Problem 688. Temporal compatibility in a story set in 1750
Knowledge context.
Anachronism can be tested as a compatibility problem when the relevant date ranges are supplied.
Given facts.

For this problem, availability intervals are: Technology A: 1200–1600; Institution B: 1500–1900; Tool C: 1700–2000; Practice D: 1300–1450. A story is set in 1750 and mentions Technology A and Tool C together. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 5 km and two checkpoints are 4 cm apart.
Rules.

An item is temporally compatible with a year only if the year lies inside its stated availability interval. An anachronism is an item placed outside its given interval. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Task.
Which mentioned item, if any, is anachronistic in the story? Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Check 1750 against Technology A interval 1200–1600. 2. Check 1750 against Tool C interval 1700–2000. 3. Items outside their intervals: ['Technology A']. Cross-domain check: 4×5=20 km.
Answer.
Anachronistic: Technology A. Cross-domain answer: 20 km.
Knowledge takeaway.
The reasoning does not require memorizing invention dates if the intervals are part of the problem.
